translationRepairs: When Gao Yan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
s0095’s 世祖踐祚 names Northern Qi Shizu (Gao Zhan / Wucheng), not Gao Yan (Xiaozhao / Suzong); replacing Gao Yan with Gao Zhan corrects the misidentification while leaving the offices intact.
When Gao Yan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
The literal field likewise misreads 世祖 as Gao Yan; Gao Zhan is the correct personal name for temple-name Shizu in this Northern Qi context.
Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with no choice in personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.
Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with irreproachable personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.

身無擇行 is the classical collocation for conduct with nothing open to censure, paired with 口無戲言; “no choice in personal conduct” is a false calque, and “irreproachable personal conduct” restores the sense.
Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with no choice in personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.
Wenji's younger brother Wenjing was diligent in study, square and refined in manner, with irreproachable personal conduct and no jesting words on his lips.
Same mistranslation of 身無擇行 in the literal field; irreproachable personal conduct matches the Chinese and the parallel 口無戲言.
In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin by the mother's side Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
從兄 denotes an elder agnatic cousin, not a maternal-side cousin (表兄); dropping “by the mother’s side” removes invented kinship detail.
He left private life for a staff post under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Xing, then rose to secretariat gentleman.
He left private life for a staff post under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang, then rose to secretariat gentleman.

太師咸陽王行參軍 is a staff post (行參軍) under the Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang; 行 is not a personal name Xing. The proposed “Grand Tutor the Prince of Xianyang” is awkward, so the revised wording removes the false Xing without the intrusive article.
He doffed the headcloth and became a staff officer under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Xing, then was promoted to secretariat gentleman.
He doffed the headcloth and became a staff officer under Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang, then was promoted to secretariat gentleman.
Literal likewise mistook 行參軍 for a name Xing; the office is acting/staff aide under the Prince of Xianyang. Revised to drop Xing while avoiding the awkward “Grand Tutor the Prince.”
In Wuping he entered the Wenslin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.
In Wuping he entered the Wenlin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.
文林館 is Wenlin Hall; “Wenslin” is a typographical corruption of the same name, and the proposed Wenlin Hall matches 文林.
In Wuping he entered the Wenslin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.
In Wuping he entered the Wenlin Hall to compile books, then went out as governor of Wude commandery.
The literal field repeats the Wenslin corruption of 文林館; Wenlin Hall is the correct transcription.
In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin by the mother's side Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
In the Wei Xiaochang era Lie's elder cousin Kan was administrator and, holding the commandery, raised troops in external rebellion.
Literal 從兄 likewise does not mean maternal cousin; removing “by the mother’s side” restores the kinship term without other changes.
His father Zigong had been Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke of Literature.
His father Zigong had been Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke Wenxian.
文獻公 is the posthumous ducal title Wenxian, not a descriptive “Duke of Literature”; Duke Wenxian correctly preserves the title compound.
His father Zigong was Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke of Literature.
His father Zigong was Wei secretariat supervisor, Minister of Works, and Duke Wenxian.
The literal field makes the same error on 文獻公; Duke Wenxian is the accurate rendering of the posthumous title.

Wenzong's younger brother Wenzju also had talent and capacity; he passed through director in the revenue section, director of the two-thousand-bushel section, and chief aide of Ding province while concurrently governing Zhongshan commandery.

Wenzong's younger brother Wenju also had talent and capacity; he passed through director in the revenue section, director of the two-thousand-bushel section, and chief aide of Ding province while concurrently governing Zhongshan commandery.
文舉 romanizes as Wenju; “Wenzju” inserts a spurious z, and the proposed Wenju matches the given name while leaving the offices unchanged.
The Zhou court made him general of the establishment of the same rank and master of the carriage office.
The Zhou court made him general of the establishment of the same rank and grand master of the Zai shi.

載師大夫 is the Northern Zhou Zai shi land-allotment grand master, not a carriage office; the proposal’s office sense is right, but title-casing the whole idiomatic sentence is awkward, so casing is kept in line with the original idiomatic style.
The Zhou court made him General of the Establishment of the Same Rank and Master of the Carriage Office.
The Zhou court made him General of the Establishment of the Same Rank and Grand Master of the Zai shi.
Literal Master of the Carriage Office misidentifies 載師; Grand Master of the Zai shi correctly names the Zhouli-derived land office in Northern Zhou nomenclature.
At the end of Qi there were also Xin Ti of Longxi, merged-bureau director in the Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
At the end of Qi there were also Xin Que of Longxi, merged-bureau director in the Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
辛愨 is Xin Que (愨 què); “Xin Ti” misreads the given name, and Xin Que restores the correct personal name without changing the rest.

At the end of Qi there were also Xin Que of Longxi, director in the merged-bureau Masters of Writing, and Pan Ziyi of Changle, regular-attendant cavalier attendant—both known for talent and capacity.
The literal field likewise mistransliterates 愨 as Ti; Xin Que is the accurate reading of 辛愨.
